terminology_notes: Ryud, Morellen, Pezik and Kaipers are provisional. Preserve the damaged epitaph's partial Ryud name. Leiden and Herengracht use standard Dutch place-name orthography; no official English game localization is claimed. English-looking journal names Jane, John and Smith do not alone establish anyone's gender.

Kigashira Mushroom and Kranrutze are provisional transliterations. De Burcht is the Dutch place-name reconstruction of the Diemen inscription; Japanese identity is confirmed at https://w.atwiki.jp/wizfan/pages/100.html . Turf is provisional Dutch spelling. Inktvis/Garnalen/Zalm/Tong/Schol are Dutch squid/shrimp/salmon/sole/plaice terms suggested by the source fish riddle; these are editorial display forms, never replacements for parser literals.

Skua, Kayuken and Balmar Guard are provisional transliterations; no matching English source located. Kramer Hat matches the inherited item database. Dutch puzzle tree names Cocosnoot, Amandel, Walnoot and Laurier retain the source's name/clue identities, cross-checked at https://w.atwiki.jp/ps3wizbourei/pages/85.html . Never silently alter parser literals to these display spellings.

Bahelmeja, Kulgar Straat and Dulong Straat are provisional transliterations; the Japanese place identity is cross-checked at https://w.atwiki.jp/ps3wizbourei/pages/96.html . No published English spelling was located.

Additional speaker spellings Riz, Anneberg, Pluton, Gate Keeper, Key Master and Cock Robin follow the bilingual credit transcription. Do not infer gender from a performer or title. English-only staff name evidence remains to be checked separately.

Names without a documented nickname, personality or gender retain null/scene-specific fields rather than fabricated biography. Puzzle boxes are descriptive speaker labels; preserve any separate accepted-input literals.
Existing official English names take priority when an actual matching term can be verified. Do not copy another translation's prose.
Dungeon/place romanizations without published English spellings are provisional; use these consistently and flag uncertain readings.
Translate natural Japanese prose. Preserve bytecode IDs, filenames, printf placeholders, @ controls and runtime substitution syntax verbatim.
Unknown character gender stays unknown until the scene supplies evidence.

Village identities cross-checked at https://w.atwiki.jp/wizfan/pages/90.html; romanizations remain provisional. Odinous is a default adventurer name, not a race; gender is not established. Strage is the provisional dungeon spelling, not Storage.
Event source identifies Anselm as Beatrix's adoptive father and Chu Lu Gah's last disciple. Preserve those relationships. Chu Lu Gah is referred to as male in E0601-E0612.

Official prior-game English race spelling Porklu is confirmed at https://steamcommunity.com/achievements/948640 . Prefer it to the earlier provisional Pookle. Prior-game boss spellings Tempestus Rex and Ala Cabra cross-checked against matching Japanese/English trophy names at https://gamefaqs.gamespot.com/ps3/981422-wizardry-labyrinth-of-lost-souls/trophies .

Invisible Solution is the shared item term; the event explicitly explains invisibility. Do not replace ordinary prose using unseen/invisible. Fenodyree follows the creature spelling in John Rhys's Celtic Folklore, Welsh and Manx.
